entries.title: Draft: Boolean coordinate split entropy profile
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. For Boolean f and a specified coordinate i, write f^+ and f^- for its two restrictions, Delta_i=H(f)-(H(f^+)+H(f^-))/2 and delta=I_i(f). Then Delta_i<=h_2(delta)+(2/ln 2)delta, where h_2 is binary entropy. This upper bound is known prior work, independently rederived here. Its binary-entropy term cannot be replaced by a universal constant times delta at every coordinate.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient

entries.title: Draft: false universal coordinate split charge
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. The stronger assertion that there exists a finite universal K such that Delta_i H(f)<=K I_i(f) for every Boolean f and every specified coordinate i is false. This assertion quantifies over every coordinate and is stronger than an induction that chooses a suitable coordinate depending on f.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient

entries.title: Draft: quadratic bent point-flip selector
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. For even n>=2, t in F_2^n, let g(t)=(-1)^(sum_{j=1}^{n/2} t_{2j-1}t_{2j}), h(t)=g(t)-2*1_{t=0}, and F(t,+1)=g(t), F(t,-1)=h(t). Both restrictions and F are Boolean. With p=2^-n, I_z(F)=p and Delta_z H(F)/p>=n-4/ln 2. Also I(F)=n/2+(n+1)p and H(F)/I(F) tends to 2. Thus this family refutes an every-coordinate linear charge, without refuting full FEI.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient

entries.title: Draft: sharp additive constant in the split profile
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. For even n>=2 use g(t)=(-1)^(sum_j t_{2j-1}t_{2j}), h=g-2*1_{t=0} and selector F(t,+1)=g(t), F(t,-1)=h(t). For p=2^-n, Delta_z H(F)/p=n+3/ln 2+O(p), whereas h_2(p)/p=n+1/ln 2+O(p). Hence [Delta_z H(F)-h_2(p)]/p tends to 2/ln 2, making the additive coefficient in Delta_i<=h_2(I_i)+(2/ln 2)I_i optimal. Multiplication by an independent dictator balances F and both restrictions while preserving their entropies and selector influence.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient

entries.title: Draft: sharp two-bit split increment bound
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. For every Boolean f and every coordinate i, 0<=H(f)-(H(f^+)+H(f^-))/2<=2 bits. The upper bound is attained by f(z,x,y)=((1+z)x+(1-z)y)/2: it has four squared Fourier coefficients equal to 1/4, restricted entropies zero, and selector influence 1/2.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient

entries.title: Draft: squared-spectrum charge obstruction
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. For even n>=2, let g(t)=(-1)^(sum_j t_{2j-1}t_{2j}), h=g-2*1_{t=0} and let F join g,h across a selector z. Put p=2^-n. Then sum_S |ghat(S)^2-hhat(S)^2|/I_z(F)=4(1-p)/sqrt(p). This disproves a universal squared-spectrum L1 charge by influence at every specified split.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient

entries.title: Draft: retain the coordinate quantifier in FEI induction
entries.statement: DRAFT: independent mathematical referee review pending; no novelty claim. A restriction induction for a Boolean class closed under restrictions needs a uniform K and, for every f in the class, existence of a coordinate i with Delta_i H(f)<=K I_i(f). The quadratic bent point-flip selector has a bad selector coordinate, but each original coordinate has influence 1/2+2^-n and split increment at most 2, so its split ratio is below 4. A specified bad coordinate cannot refute this existential premise.
assumptions: Base-2 Fourier entropy including the empty coefficient
Class closed under restrictions for the proposed induction

relations.rationale: The Boolean specified-split ratio exceeds every fixed K as even n grows.
The sharpness limit uses the exact Boolean selector family.
The family approaches the additive constant in the stated upper profile.
The squared-spectrum obstruction is computed on the same explicitly defined family.
Its specified bad coordinate leaves all original coordinate ratios below 4.
The two-bit bound supplies the good-coordinate ratio bound.
